precepts.text: There were in the church that was at Antioch certain prophets and teachers; as Barnabas, and Simeon that was called Niger. It was never derogatory.
precepts.point: The word of the Lord that came to Micah the Morasthite: the word Moor, Morasthite, is in the Bible. Micah, teacher of the Moors.
precepts.why:
“Now there were in the church that was at Antioch certain prophets and teachers; as Barnabas, and Simeon that was called Niger”. Right there among the prophets and teachers of the church is a man called Niger. It was never derogatory. It was a name for our people, used in the church itself, set alongside Barnabas, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen and Saul.

That is the same thing as Micah the Morasthite in Micah 1:1. The word Moor is in the Bible: Micah, teacher of the Moors. These names were ours, and they described our people plainly. The names that came later were put on us by others: the Latins, who later became the Romans, gave the name Africa to the region around Carthage and Utica. Africa was a term that came way later.

So we have to go back to the name God calls us. Simeon called Niger and Micah the Morasthite were Israelites, teachers and prophets of our people, and the scriptures show them to us by those names without any shame in them.

precepts.text: Micah the Morasthite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah: Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps.
precepts.point: The word of the Lord that came to Micah the Morasthite: the word Moor, Morasthite, is in the Bible. Micah, teacher of the Moors.
precepts.why:
Jeremiah names the same prophet: “Micah the Morasthite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and spake to all the people of Judah, saying, Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of a forest.”

It confirms Micah 1:1: the word of the Lord came to Micah the Morasthite in the days of Hezekiah, king of Judah, and it was a word against Jerusalem. Morasthite: the Moor is in the Bible, and Micah was a teacher of the Moors.

And what Micah prophesied is what happened to us, over and over. Anytime we are set somewhere, we rise up as a nation, and the Lord allows Esau to conquer us. Why? Because the savior is Christ. If we could do it without Christ, why would we need Christ? The Moors went into Europe in 710 AD and brought universities, soap, the holy waters that became rubbing alcohol, strawberries, olives and grapes, wine, even chess; then they were conquered and scattered, many sent to Africa and transported to Brazil and North America. Zion plowed like a field, Jerusalem become heaps.

precepts.text: Then Solomon began to build the house of the Lord at Jerusalem in mount Moriah, where the Lord appeared unto David his father. Moriah: Moor right there, black again. The hill of the Moors was part of Jerusalem.
precepts.point: The word of the Lord that came to Micah the Morasthite: the word Moor, Morasthite, is in the Bible. Micah, teacher of the Moors.
precepts.why:
This shows that the hill of the Morasthites was part of Jerusalem: “Then Solomon began to build the house of the Lord at Jerusalem in mount Moriah, where the Lord appeared unto David his father, in the place that David had prepared in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite.” Moriah: Moor right there, black again.

The reference work read in class says the same. Moriah was a hill adjacent to Jerusalem, on the northeast. There Abraham offered his son, in Genesis 22, and when Solomon built the temple on it, it became included in the city.

So the temple of the Lord stood on the hill of the Moors, and Micah the Morasthite, the teacher of the Moors, was a prophet of that same people. The Moors were Israelites; the names Moors and Africa came later, but the land and the house of the Lord tie them to Jerusalem.

precepts.text: Micah, prophesying in the same time, says the Most High will make Samaria a heap, pouring down her stones and laying her idols desolate.
precepts.point: Because their rage and tumult came up to His ears, the Most High will put His hook in Sennacherib's nose and His bridle in his lips, and turn him back the way he came, which joins with the blast promised in verse 7.

note.label: 2 Kings 19: The Most High Defends Jerusalem

precepts.why:
Micah prophesied in the same time: “Therefore I will make Samaria as an heap of the field, and as plantings of a vineyard: and I will pour down the stones thereof into the valley, and I will discover the foundations thereof.” Samaria is made a heap and her idols laid desolate.

That is the work the Most High formed of ancient times and brought to pass through Assyria, “that thou shouldest be to lay waste fenced cities into ruinous heaps.” Samaria fell to Assyria by his hand. Yet when Assyria raged against him and came against Jerusalem, the virgin the daughter of Zion “hath despised thee, and laughed thee to scorn.” Israel laughs at the enemy, for it is already written that they lose.
